name: Stirling-PDF
summary: A locally hosted one-stop shop for all your PDF needs
description: Stirling-PDF is a robust, locally hosted web-based PDF manipulation tool using Docker. It enables you to carry out various operations on PDF files, including splitting, merging, converting, reorganizing, adding images, rotating, compressing, and more. This locally hosted web application has evolved to encompass a comprehensive set of features, addressing all your PDF requirements.

Stirling Office Convert has now replaced Libreoffice in our docker containers!
Along with speed increases and better quality conversions it also means our docker going to half the size! Thank you to everyone who sent us example files, and please keep reporting any conversions that don't look right! We are hoping to get this perfect!
We have also made a big fix for desktop users whose documents were reloading a few seconds after upload, Thank you to everyone who reported this and great to see people using the new feedback button! (In bottom right)
With the Office Convert change (outside of the tools getting the toggle removed)
- Compress now uses Office Convert
- HTML to PDF supports zoom again
- New admin setting to cap how many Office conversions run at once and queue
- Damaged Office, ebook and HTML files now give a clear "could not be read" message instead of an error
Other changes are:
- Faster desktop PDF operations, with the PDF engine now pre-installed in the app
- Performance improvements across the viewer, file list etc
- JPDFium and other dependency updates causing various bug fixes and improvements
We also fixed some bugs including:
- Desktop documents reloading themselves and losing progress shortly after being opened
- Filled form fields showing their value twice in the viewer
- Form values being invisible in dark mode
- Thumbnail sidebar getting stuck on "Loading..." after applying changes
Note (breaking changes):
- PDF to .doc (Word 97-2003) output has been removed. Use docx or odt instead; API calls, pipelines and automations asking for doc will now return an error
- .wpd, .wps, .lwp, .abw, .hwp and .xps files are no longer accepted for conversion
- groupsToRemove entries for removed tools (LibreOffice, Calibre, Weasyprint, OpenCV, etc.) no longer disable anything.

A big release! Lots of changes in this release around the PDF Text Editor, such as it now works directly inside the viewer by clicking the edit text button in the top bar.
Other changes for it include:
- It can use fonts from the server including any custom provided fonts that are placed in customFiles/static/fonts/.
- It does a much better job of matching scanned (OCRed) documents to their fonts
- Brand new font picker for those OCR scenarios
- General text editor fixes for typed text and lag issues
- Embedded fonts are now subset, so saved files are smaller.
Other features in this release include:
- OneDrive support has been added to our pro plan with more to come soon
- Brand new check PDF accessibility tool which checks PDFs against PDF/UA-1 or PDF/UA-2 and generates reports (More to come soon!)
- New setup wizard for new server setups to help onboard users easier
- Enterprise users get SCIM 2.0 user provisioning
- Admins concerned about users editting and invalidating signatures can now disable users from doing that, this also comes with a new signature detection interface
Other changes are:
- New settings menu submenu with easy access logout button
- Custom page size option for Scale Pages
- New “Clear recents” button in the file sidebar
- Odd-even merge in Reorganize Pages
- Pixel comparison mode is back in the Compare tool
- Metadata updates can now keep the fields you leave out (keepOmitted=true)
- The feedback button is back (admins can turn it off with system.enableFeedback: false)
- Faster desktop startup with large temp folders and on first launch
- Desktop keeps open files locked on Windows so a DMS doesn’t check them in
- Lots of dependency updates
We also fixed some bugs including:
- Page numbers being placed wrong on rotated and cropped pages
- Uploads from Safari not always sending correctly
- A held-back file drop leaving the desktop UI stuck
- MCP convert tool missing its convert operation, and AI engine errors not showing as MCP tool errors
This release also includes several security and stability improvements
Note: the PostScript vector conversion endpoints have been removed (/convert/vector/pdf for PS/EPS to PDF, and /convert/pdf/vector for PDF to PS/EPS/PCL/XPS)

Stirling Office Convert (still beta) has been upgraded. You can also now pick it as the converter in lots of other tools such as Email, HTML, Markdown and ebooks to PDF plus PDF to HTML/Markdown/XML/EPUB/AZW3, and PDF/A. Please compare it with the existing converter and let us know!
Our roadmap is to turn Office Convert on by default next week, and then, if no changes are required, fully remove LibreOffice and other dependencies the week after. So now is the best time to try it and report (And send example files) any conversions that don't look correct!
Other changes are:
- SSO auto-login now works even when username/password login is enabled (admins can still reach the password form via /login?all)
- JPDFium upgrade and support and Windows ARM64 support, This update also brings better redaction, merge/split improvements and lower memory on big files
- Faster and more accurate mobile scanning, with no more 9MB OpenCV bundled
- Faster requests with far fewer database reads and new entity caching
- Quieter startup and runtime logs
- Spring Boot, Docker base image and lots of other dependency updates
- Updated translations for all languages
We also fixed some bugs including
- Convert sending multiple or mixed file uploads to the wrong conversion
- Ebook settings resetting the selected output format
- "Include all recipients" not controlling CC/BCC in email to PDF
- PDF/UA font embedding making form fields no longer fillable
- Certificate signing rejecting unencrypted PKCS#8 PEM keys
- Viewer jumping away from your page after adding a bookmark
- Archive extraction being offered for non-zip files
This release also includes several security and stability improvements, so we advise users to update when possible!
Note: the old, deprecated backend PDF text editing API has been removed in favour of the new Text Editor. We are hoping to add a new Text Editor API soon!

Stirling PDF V3.0 is live!
With this update we are introducing a lot of exciting new changes, A brand new automation system, Free OAuth SSO for all, brand new text editor and a ton of new features, bug fixes and security fixes
We have a new system along side the "PDF Editor" called the "PDF Processor"
The PDF Processor takes the tools you already use in Stirling PDF and lets you run them across a large numbers of files with a variety of sources (Folders/FTP/S3 etc)
The idea is, If you need to OCR 10,000 files, Compress a whole folder or convert a whole document library this should be a tool which can help with that and allow it to listen and run for future files as they arrive
This is the first major release of Processor and we will be improving it quickly based on how people use it.
Full Processor guide with examples
AI is also available as an optional part of Processor.
You can use AI to understand documents, classify them, extract information, and help automate processing. AI is fully optional (and off by default) and can use various models including locally/self-hosted models depending on your setup.
Automation now includes 1,000 PDFs per month free.
This allowance applies to automated processing through Processor, API, and AI features.
Linking your server to stirling.com gives you an additional 500 PDFs per month and access to our hosted AI (If you dont want to host your own).
Normal PDF Editor usage remains free and unlimited. In addition, we are also making OAuth SSO free for all users.
V3.0 also includes major improvements to the PDF Editor side of things:
- The already mentioned free OAuth SSO
- Brand new Text Editor, now out of alpha you should expect drastic better UI, performance and compatibility

- QR code splitting not working for certain PDFs

- Redact UI issues
